children: The European Central Bank's decision to increase interest rates protects against high energy prices extending into wages and services prices, eToro's Lale Akoner says in a note. The ECB increased the deposit rate to 2.5% during Thursday's policy decision, as widely expected. "Still, higher rates can limit how far the energy shock spreads through the economy, but they cannot address its underlying cause," Akoner says. The ECB risks hurting European households' spending power due to higher interest rates, she says. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)
